title: Kuwait protests to Iran as Italy says drone that killed two Italians was Iranian-made
dek: Kuwait summoned Iran's ambassador after the attack on a military site; Tehran denies involvement and offers to join an inquiry. The US says it disabled a ship running its blockade of Iranian ports.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Kuwait on Friday summoned Iran's ambassador and handed him a written protest over what it called "continuing Iranian attacks", a day after a drone struck a Kuwaiti military site and killed two Italian technicians. Italy's foreign minister, Antonio Tajani, said Kuwaiti investigators had established that the drone was made in Iran. Tehran denies any role and has offered to join a commission of inquiry with Italy and Kuwait.

The diplomatic row came as the confrontation at sea around Iran sharpened. The US military said its aircraft disabled a Palau-flagged merchant ship in the Gulf of Oman on Thursday after it tried to break the American blockade of Iranian ports, and Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two oil tankers using what they called an "unauthorised" route through the Strait of Hormuz had run into trouble, one of them hitting a naval mine. For India, which buys most of its crude from the Gulf and whose citizens form the largest foreign community in Kuwait, each new incident adds to the risk of higher oil prices and to the safety concerns of workers in the region.

## What happened in Kuwait

Kuwait's defence ministry said its armed forces detected hostile drones in the country's airspace on Thursday, and that one hit what officials described as a "vital site", according to reports. The two Italians killed were technicians employed by Rheinmetall Italia, the Italian arm of the German defence group Rheinmetall, who were maintaining radar equipment for an air defence system, reports said. A Kuwaiti and a Pakistani national were injured by falling shrapnel, and the site suffered extensive damage. Kuwaiti officials have not said publicly which facility was hit.

On Friday, Kuwait's deputy foreign minister, Hamad Sulaiman Al-Mishaan, called in the Iranian ambassador, Mohammad Totonji, and gave him a protest note. He said the attacks were a "violation of Kuwait's sovereignty and territorial integrity", breached international law and the UN Charter, and that Kuwait held Iran fully responsible, according to reports of the statement.

Mr Tajani said: "According to the investigations carried out by the Kuwaitis, the drone was manufactured in Iran." He added that this did not necessarily mean it had been launched from Iranian territory or by Iranian forces, noting that several Iran-backed groups in the region also use Iranian-made drones, according to reports. He said Italy and Kuwait would investigate, and that Iran had said it was ready to take part.

## What Iran says

Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, called the attack "suspicious", denied that the drone came from Iran or was launched by Iranian forces, and proposed a joint commission to establish who was responsible, according to reports. A spokesman for Iran's armed forces, Abolfazl Shekarchi, said Iranian forces had carried out no offensive operations in the region and accused the United States and Israel of "false-flag" tactics, reports said. None of these accounts could be independently verified.

Saudi Arabia and Syria were among the governments that blamed Iran, and the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation condemned the attack, according to reports.

## At sea: a ship disabled and claims of mines

US Central Command said its aircraft fired "precision munitions" at the stern of the M/V Pacific Archer in the Gulf of Oman on Thursday, disabling its propulsion, and that "the civilian crew was unharmed", according to reports. US officials said the ship had left the Iranian port of Bandar Abbas before trying to run the blockade; ship-tracking sites listed its destination as Singapore. Central Command said its forces give several warnings before firing on merchant vessels.

The United States says it has turned back 158 merchant ships since July and disables those that refuse to comply. The Pacific Archer is at least the 15th vessel it has publicly said it disabled since April, and the sixth since July; the previous one was on 7 November, according to reports.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Friday that two tankers had tried to cross the Strait of Hormuz by an "unauthorised" route, and that one hit a naval mine and the other turned back, according to reports. In a later account, the Guards said two tankers "caught fire and exploded" after hitting mines near Oman's Khasab port and in the eastern part of the strait. Neither the ships nor their owners were named, and the claims have not been independently confirmed. Iran's navy commander, Shahram Irani, said on state television that Iran would carry out operations that would "not only break the naval blockade but also drive the enemy out of the region's waters", reports said.

Earlier this week the Guards made a similar claim about three tankers, which the Joint Maritime Information Centre, run by Western navies, said was unconfirmed.

## Background

The United States has blockaded Iranian ports since April. It lifted the blockade temporarily during talks with Tehran and reimposed it in July, and keeps a large naval force in the region, including two aircraft carriers. Iran has responded by tightening its own restrictions on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, through which a large share of the world's seaborne oil passes, and on Monday its army commander ordered the closure to be tightened "further day by day" until Washington meets Tehran's conditions for a settlement.

At the same time, Saudi Arabia has come under repeated drone and missile attack. Yemen's Houthi movement, which is aligned with Iran, has claimed strikes on three Saudi refineries in five days, including Ras Tanura, the kingdom's largest; a projectile hit Aramco's Jazan refinery on Thursday and killed a Nepali worker. Brent crude was trading close to $97 a barrel on Friday and was heading for its first weekly rise this month, and India's Sensex fell 989 points on the oil worries.

## Why it matters for India

India imports most of its crude oil, much of it from Gulf producers whose cargoes pass the Strait of Hormuz, so disruption there feeds directly into import costs, the rupee and fuel prices. Indians are also the largest expatriate community in Kuwait and across the Gulf, and the Gulf's shipping lanes carry Indian seafarers. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, hosting Indian Ocean Rim Association ministers in Delhi on Friday, called attacks on shipping and seafarers "simply unacceptable".

## What happens next

Italy and Kuwait say they will continue their investigation, and it is not yet clear whether Iran will be allowed to join it. Kuwait has not said whether it will take further diplomatic steps beyond the protest note. At sea, the US has given no sign of easing the blockade, while Iran says it will try to break it; shipping insurers and oil traders will be watching whether the claimed mine strikes are confirmed.

## Key numbers

- 2: Italian technicians killed in the drone strike in Kuwait on Thursday
- 2: people injured, a Kuwaiti and a Pakistani national
- 15th: vessel the US says it has disabled since April, the Pacific Archer
- 158: merchant ships the US says it has turned back since July
- About $97: Brent crude price on Friday
